notes.meaning: David cries out to God in desperate trouble, begging Him to come quickly to his rescue. He uses both the title God and the covenant name, the LORD, showing his earnest faith. When people face sudden danger, God welcomes their urgent and honest pleas for help.

other.label: Modern scholarship
other.view: Some scholars debate whether this psalm was originally an independent prayer later joined to Psalm 40, though most view it as a detached fragment taken from Psalm 40 for liturgical use.

notes.meaning: David asks God to stop his enemies and turn them back in confusion. These attackers were hunting for his life and cheering for his ruin. David trusts that God will defend him by causing the plots of wicked people to fail.

Cruel enemies mocked David during his trouble, shouting taunts to show their deep contempt. David prays that their wicked jeering will backfire and cover them with disgrace instead. God sees when the afflicted are ridiculed, and He does not allow such arrogance to stand.

Even in the middle of his own danger, David prays for the joy of the whole community of faith. He asks that everyone who seeks God and loves His salvation will be filled with gladness. True worshippers look beyond their own trials to praise God and declare His greatness.

David ends with an honest confession, admitting that he is poor, needy, and completely unable to save himself. He looks to God as his only true helper and rescuer. Because his danger is urgent, he boldly pleads with the Lord not to delay.
